evidence: pyproject.toml declares 190+ production dependencies, including multiple overlapping libraries: bleach (HTML sanitization) and nh3 (HTML sanitization) both present — nh3 seen used in checkinlists/exporters.py; bleach may be redundant.
orjson and standard json are both present — orjson seen used in some serializers, json used in many views/services, but no consistent policy on which to prefer.
PyJWT (pyjwt) and jwcrypto both present — jwt used in eventyay_common/utils.py and base/models/event.py; jwcrypto likely used for WebAuthn but is heavy for that purpose.
pandas listed as a dependency (heavy ML/data library); usage appears limited to analytics graphs (features/analytics/graphs/utils.py) which could use lighter alternatives.
matplotlib listed as a dependency — also potentially only for analytics charts.
Both requests and aiohttp present — HTTP clients for sync vs async paths, which is expected in a mixed sync/ASGI app but worth monitoring.
vat-moss-forked pinned with note 'Hold back by eventyay-stripe' and comment 'This library prevents us from being compatible with Python v3.13+' — version conflict actively blocking Python upgrade.
pyproject.toml uses >= version specifiers for all dependencies (no upper bounds), making reproducible builds dependent entirely on the lock mechanism.
eventyay-paypal, eventyay-stripe, eventyay-bitpay, exhibition all pinned to @main branches of GitHub repos — unpinned upstream main branches introduce silent breakage risk.
pdf2image and pdfrw both present for PDF handling alongside reportlab — three PDF libraries for potentially overlapping use cases.
bleach and nh3 both present for HTML sanitization — nh3 is the newer Rust-based replacement for bleach; having both suggests incomplete migration.

strengths: Core framework dependencies (Django, DRF, Celery, Channels) are sensibly organized and on recent versions.
Dev dependencies are cleanly separated into [dependency-groups] dev section.
External payment plugins are isolated as separate packages, keeping payment logic out of the core dependency graph.
The comment about vat-moss-forked blocking Python 3.13 shows the team is aware of the constraint and has documented it.
dependency_health.issue_character: The dominant issue is dependency surface bloat: multiple libraries serving the same purpose (bleach+nh3, orjson+json, pyjwt+jwcrypto, pdf2image+pdfrw+reportlab, requests+aiohttp) combined with heavy analytics dependencies (pandas, matplotlib) and four upstream-pinned-to-@main external plugins.
dependency_health.score_rationale: The codebase carries substantial dependency health risk. The bleach/nh3 dual HTML sanitizer and the active version conflict blocking Python 3.13 are the most concrete defects. The four @main-pinned plugins create silent breakage risk on every pip install. The 190+ flat dependency list with no upper bounds makes auditing difficult. This is materially worse than a healthy project, which would have consolidated sanitizers, explicit commit hashes for git-sourced deps, and a single JSON serializer policy, warranting a score in the low-50s range.

issues.summary: bleach and nh3 both declared as dependencies for HTML sanitization — incomplete migration
evidence: "bleach>=6.3.0" and "nh3>=0.3.2" both appear in dependencies
nh3 is used in app/eventyay/plugins/checkinlists/exporters.py
bleach is the legacy library nh3 is designed to replace
issues.suggestion: Audit all bleach usages, migrate to nh3, and remove bleach from pyproject.toml.

issues.summary: Four external plugins pinned to @main Git branches with no commit hash, creating silent breakage risk
evidence: "eventyay-paypal @ git+https://github.com/fossasia/eventyay-paypal.git@main"
"eventyay-stripe @ git+https://github.com/fossasia/eventyay-stripe.git@main"
"eventyay-bitpay @ git+https://github.com/fossasia/eventyay-bitpay.git@main"
"exhibition @ git+https://github.com/fossasia/eventyay-exhibition.git@main"
issues.suggestion: Pin each git dependency to a specific commit SHA (e.g., @abc1234) or create tagged releases and use version ranges. This ensures reproducible installs and prevents upstream main-branch changes from breaking builds.

issues.summary: vat-moss-forked dependency blocks Python 3.13+ compatibility, documented but unresolved
evidence: requires-python = ">=3.12, <3.13"
Comment: "# This library prevents us from being compatible with Python v3.13+."
issues.suggestion: Evaluate whether vat-moss-forked can be replaced with pyvat (already in deps) or vat_moss directly, or vendor the specific EU VAT validation functions used to eliminate the blocker.

issues.summary: pandas and matplotlib pulled in for analytics charts — heavy data-science libraries for a web app
evidence: "pandas>=2.3.3" and "matplotlib>=3.10.8" in production dependencies
Seed files reference app/eventyay/features/analytics/graphs/utils.py suggesting chart generation is the primary use
issues.suggestion: Audit actual pandas/matplotlib usage in analytics; if only simple chart generation is needed, consider lighter alternatives (e.g., Pillow + manual drawing, or chart.js on the frontend) to reduce install size and startup overhead.

issues.summary: Three PDF-related libraries present (pdf2image, pdfrw, reportlab) with overlapping capabilities
evidence: "pdf2image>=1.17.0", "pdfrw>=0.4", "reportlab>=4.4.9" all in dependencies
reportlab used in plugins/checkinlists/exporters.py for PDF generation
issues.suggestion: Audit which PDF operations each library handles; consolidate where possible (reportlab already handles PDF generation; pdf2image adds rasterization, pdfrw adds manipulation — confirm each is truly needed).

root_causes: Merger of two codebases (pretix + pretalx) brought together two sets of dependencies that were not consolidated
Incremental addition of analytics features added heavy data-science libraries without evaluating lighter alternatives
Using @main git pins for payment plugins suggests the plugins are developed in tandem and released informally
likely_symptoms: dual_html_sanitizer — symptom of in-progress migration from bleach to nh3 that was not completed
possible_false_positives: requests + aiohttp dual HTTP clients — justified by mixed sync/async (Django + Channels/Celery) architecture
